response.markdown_report:
The strongest next step remains a **terminal-mask supervision allocation pilot** within corrected BERT4Rec. At 20% research progress, this is a feasible experiment, but terminal supervision is established practice: the contribution is a controlled allocation study, with explicit supervision accounting.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have measured negative-wins rates of 12.25% and 11.27%. These training-pair measurements identify weaker separation, without establishing validation performance. (2) Alignment scores near 0.51 imply mean embedding cosines near zero, providing little evidence of directional collapse. (3) Serving-parity gates and disjoint-user patch confirmation support controlled diagnosis. Intervention effects nevertheless cannot establish users’ current needs.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) already includes terminal-only masking; its one-mask ablation does not isolate terminal selection. (2) The [official generator](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py) and [loss](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py#L327-L366) distinguish example frequency from target weighting: ten random examples plus one terminal example give 1/11 dedicated terminal examples, but only 1/(10k+1) dedicated terminal targets when random examples contain k targets. (3) [Zhang and Nanda](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042) show localization depends on corruption and metrics; retain bounded patching as supporting evidence. (4) [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939) motivates holding optimization fixed, while [Recency Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) motivates distinguishing endpoint selection from masking allocation.

**Framework and directions.**

| Direction | Evidence | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Objective alignment | Matched interior/terminal training-prefix ranks; target counts and loss reduction | Whether supervision allocation improves validation |
| History dependence | Recent/older perturbations and residual patches | Whether dependence is useful |
| Evidence sufficiency | Public titles, descriptions, timestamps | Compatibility and current intent remain uncertain |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment includes a benefit and limitation.

- **Terminal-mask mixture: 2/6/4.** Originality: a controlled task-specific allocation test, but established masking. Potential: directly tests serving alignment, but bundles target count and context changes. Difficulty: localized sampler change, but loss accounting and leakage checks require care.
- **Matched interior-versus-terminal audit: 4/6/4.** Originality: useful matched comparisons, but conventional paired evaluation. Potential: separates reconstruction from serving behavior, without directly improving recommendations. Difficulty: reuses interfaces, but requires matched targets and user-level uncertainty.
- **Bidirectional patch confirmation: 5/6/6.** Originality: recommender-specific restoration/disruption controls, derived from existing patching. Potential: identifies intervention effects, with limited semantic interpretation. Difficulty: feasible frozen-model hooks, complicated by donor matching and multiplicity.
- **Single-target allocation control: 3/7/4.** Originality: isolates supervision count using established methods. Potential: clarifies allocation effects, while terminal position, recency and right-context availability remain coupled. Difficulty: simple masking, but requires an additional budgeted trial.

**Selected algorithm.** Predeclare q=0.5: mix terminal-only and corrected-baseline reconstruction examples. Within each category, sample eligible users uniformly, then endpoints uniformly from positions with nonempty preceding context; use the same endpoint/window policy in both branches. For terminal examples, retain the latest maxlen−1 preceding items, append reserved MASK, and supervise that position. For reconstruction examples, apply the corrected baseline sampler to the matched window ending at that target. This operational allocation experiment does not isolate a single causal mechanism or encode compatibility.

```text
sample training user u and endpoint t uniformly as specified
window = history[u][max(0,t-maxlen+1):t+1]
with probability 0.5:
    input = left_pad(window[:-1] + [MASK])
    supervise final MASK with window[-1]
otherwise:
    apply corrected baseline masked-target sampler(window)
optimize unchanged baseline loss and reduction
```

Retain baseline architecture, optimizer, negative sampling and loss reduction; record their exact configuration. Report examples, supervised targets, updates, GPU time, and loss reduction. If random examples average K targets, the dedicated terminal-target fraction is approximately q/[q+(1−q)K], excluding terminal selections in random examples; it is not a gradient-share estimate. If affordable, compare one terminal target against one uniformly selected real position on identical windows, with MASK replacement and one-target losses fixed. This controls target count, while right-context and position differences remain explicit.

Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches/epoch; retain routing, one checkpoint per category, diagnostic contracts, final-nonpadding readout and matching predictor writer. Repeated earlier occurrences of a target are legitimate history; report their prevalence and stratify diagnostic results rather than deleting them from training. Supplement with training-prefix popularity/length strata, shuffled histories and removed-position sensitivity checks; these do not prove shortcut removal.

Select only by unchanged host macro validation HR@10. Predeclare one mixture trial against the supplied baseline, the baseline checkpoint-evaluation cadence, and baseline retention on ties; treat gains of at most 0.005 as uncertain and do not expand search around them. Log every evaluated checkpoint. If host per-user hits are available, report a paired, category-stratified user-bootstrap interval; otherwise omit it. Fixed-candidate intervals exclude training/candidate randomness and do not correct selection bias ([Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Sampled ranking conclusions remain protocol-specific ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). No validation improvement has been measured.

idea.description: Test a preregistered 0.5 mixture of terminal-only and corrected-baseline masked-reconstruction examples within BERT4Rec, explicitly accounting for example frequency, supervised-target counts and loss reduction. Train one independent model per category in each trial.
idea.motivation: Terminal-only supervision is already part of BERT4Rec. The research question is whether changing its allocation improves the fixed RecHarness validation objective. Existing training-pair diagnostics justify investigation but do not demonstrate objective mismatch, shortcut learning or validation gains.
idea.implementation_notes: Use the supplied corrected baseline rather than assuming the official implementation describes the host. Record its masking allocation, target-selection probability, replacement rule, loss reduction and checkpoint cadence. For the proposed sampler, uniformly sample eligible users and then training endpoints with preceding context; both branches use the same window policy. Set q=0.5 before evaluation. Preserve architecture, optimizer, loss reduction and negative sampling, documenting that the operational intervention changes supervision count and available context as well as terminal allocation. Log realized counts; dedicated terminal-target share is approximately q/(q+(1-q)*E[K]), excluding terminal targets selected by reconstruction. Do not interpret target shares as gradient shares. An optional separately budgeted control uses exactly one terminal versus one uniformly sampled nonpadding target per matched window, always replacing the supervised position with MASK. This controls target count but still couples position, recency and right-context availability. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum epochs 200 and 200 batches per epoch. Retain all four categories, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, single-GPU execution and exactly one independently trained checkpoint per category at inference. Never combine baseline and intervention scores. Preserve predictor-writer consistency and DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and ModelView interfaces. Preserve masked-only supervision, reserved tokens and final-nonpadding MASK readout. Earlier repeated target IDs may remain as legitimate history; measure their prevalence without changing splits or deleting interactions. Use public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps only. Keep the bounded residual-patching pilot and matched-prefix audit supplementary. Predeclare the primary baseline comparison, retain baseline checkpoint-evaluation cadence, retain baseline on ties, flag absolute macro HR@10 gains of at most 0.005 as uncertain, and avoid adaptive expansion around tiny gains. This threshold is an operational search rule, not a significance guarantee. Log every configuration and checkpoint. Use optional paired bootstrap only when the host exposes per-user hits; never alter its evaluator. No results are claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
set preprocessing_seed=0; training_seed=42
predeclare q=0.5, primary comparison, checkpoint cadence and tie rule
for category in the four supplied categories:
    initialize supplied corrected BERT4Rec
    record baseline sampler, optimizer, loss and loss reduction
    for epoch in range(at_most_200):
        for batch_index in range(200):
            for example in batch:
                sample uniformly an eligible training user u
                sample uniformly t in {1,...,len(history[u])-1}
                window = history[u][max(0,t-maxlen+1):t+1]
                if seeded_random() < q:
                    sequence = left_pad(window[:-1] + [MASK], maxlen)
                    positive = zeros(maxlen)
                    positive[final_nonpadding_index(sequence)] = window[-1]
                    negative = baseline_negative_sampler(positive)
                else:
                    sequence, positive, negative = corrected_baseline_masked_example(window)
                assert supervised positions contain reserved MASK
                assert labels and sampled negatives use valid real-item IDs
                record example counts and supervised-target counts by branch
            update one model with unchanged baseline loss reduction and optimizer
        use unchanged authorized checkpoint-selection procedure
    export one selected checkpoint and compatible embedded predictor
    run architecture-aware diagnostics through preserved ModelView interfaces
compare models only using host macro validation HR@10
if host per-user hit indicators are available:
    for bootstrap replicate in range(2000):
        within each category, resample 200 user indices with replacement
        use identical resampled indices for baseline and intervention
        compute equally weighted mean of four category hit-rate differences
    report observed macro difference and percentile 95% interval
    state interval is conditional on models/candidates and descriptive after selection
else:
    report aggregate comparison without paired uncertainty

originality.positive: Explicit supervision accounting and matched window policies make this a useful controlled study of the supplied baseline.
originality.negative: BERT4Rec already includes terminal masking; changing its mixture probability is a hyperparameter intervention rather than a new objective.

future_potential.positive: A low-cost allocation experiment can guide whether more controlled objective-alignment research deserves the remaining budget.
future_potential.negative: Any gain may reflect target weighting, context availability or endpoint selection; it would not establish compatibility reasoning or removal of exposure bias.

code_difficulty.positive: The primary change is confined to sampling and measurement, leaving the trained architecture and serving computation intact.
code_difficulty.negative: Reproducible window matching, target accounting, baseline loss preservation and diagnostic compatibility require more care than a simple probability change.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item modeling and includes terminal-only masking for next-item recommendation.
Provides masking and component ablations relevant to supervision allocation.
limitations: Terminal supervision is prior art, so its introduction cannot support an originality claim.
The one-mask ablation does not isolate terminal versus random masking, and mask-rate changes also alter visible context.

related_work.title: Official BERT4Rec training-example generator
contributions: Generates dupe_factor randomly masked examples plus one terminal-only example per sequence window.
Separates target-selection probability from MASK-replacement probability.
limitations: Official defaults do not establish the supplied host baseline's actual configuration.
Example proportions do not equal supervised-target proportions or gradient shares.

related_work.title: Official BERT4Rec loss implementation
contributions: Pools losses over real masked targets and divides by their total count.
Shows why unequal target counts can change example weighting.
limitations: Its target-pooled reduction differs from equal weighting of per-sequence mean losses.
Changing reduction alongside masking would introduce an additional experimental factor.

related_work.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
contributions: Shows that corruption choices and evaluation metrics affect activation-patching conclusions.
Motivates controlled interventions and explicit score-based measurements.
limitations: Does not establish that recommender patching predicts validation improvement.
Intervention effects do not establish natural semantic pathways or user intent.

related_work.title: gSASRec study of overconfidence in sequential recommendation
contributions: Investigates overconfidence associated with sampled binary cross-entropy.
Motivates treating loss and sampling as potential confounders.
limitations: Does not directly establish behavior in the supplied BERT4Rec baseline.
Provides no evidence that terminal-mask reallocation improves this benchmark.

related_work.title: Recency Sampling for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Examines training-target selection and alignment with next-item prediction.
Motivates controlling endpoint sampling when comparing supervision policies.
limitations: Does not isolate the proposed BERT4Rec terminal-mask mixture.
Recency selection and right-context removal remain distinct experimental factors.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can differ materially from full-catalog metrics.
Supports interpreting benchmark results under their actual candidate protocol.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the pinned host evaluator.
Fixed negatives improve comparability without eliminating sampling bias.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how optimizing noisy selection criteria introduces selection bias.
Motivates limiting and logging adaptive configuration and checkpoint search.
limitations: Does not supply a universally appropriate improvement threshold for this benchmark.
Ordinary bootstrap intervals after selection do not remove selection bias.

related_work.title: Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
contributions: Provides precedent for paired bootstrap resampling of evaluation units.
Motivates preserving paired outcomes when estimating model differences.
limitations: Category-stratified recommender resampling is an adaptation of the method.
User bootstrap intervals conditional on fitted models and fixed candidates exclude training and candidate-resampling uncertainty.
